E03 compares the learned allocator with the real label-free ThresholdAllocator at identical verifier calls (750 at 25%). Paired CI for learned minus threshold admitted rate is [+0.412, +0.491], favoring the fixed rule. L3a, L3b and L3s agree. The threshold has no information advantage, so claim 2 is not_supported and the confound is controlled (W2 false). Claim 3: only E01 shows a small embedding AUC gain and a neighbor ratio near 1.0. Every later entry reuses the same model, task and proxy, so none qualifies as a second setting for a kill. No entry shows a gain of 0.05 or more, or a neighbor ratio of 1.5 or more. Claim 3 is open and W3 is false.

E03 runs the real LearnedAllocator against the label-free ThresholdAllocator at identical 750 verifier calls. The paired bootstrap on admitted rate (learned minus threshold) is [+0.412, +0.491], so the fixed rule wins. The baseline has no free labels, so claim 2 is not_supported, and L3a and L3i agree. For claim 3, every post-E01 entry reuses E01's pool, so none qualifies as a kill. L3k shows embeddings add -0.002 AUC and a 0.60 embedding-only AUC, which is not a supporting gain. Claim 3 stays open. W2 is false because the confound was controlled. W3 is false because no supported conclusion is held.
